Senses.Explanation: A noun for a very short interval. The corpus measures events within “one instant,” compares three years to “the interval of an instant,” and states directly that an instant is swift as a finger-snap. In expository passages it is the unit in the sequence “the previous instant ceases; the next instant arises,” while other records contrast awakening “in an instant” with wandering for myriad ages. Chan deployment repeatedly makes this inherited time-word the smallest stated interval for a change, contrast, or event. The texts do not make it a title or person, and the differing events assigned to the interval are readings of the same time-unit rather than separate senses.
Senses.Note: No master-specific or title/person sense was found. The entry describes the unit and its attested comparisons; it adds no claim beyond those comparisons.

Occurrences.Kwic: 匪用剎那之力。頓獲玄珠
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Record of the Source-Mirror says it does not require even an instant's effort before the next clause, “suddenly obtain the dark pearl.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 此流水。剎那生滅。前剎那滅。後剎那生
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An explicit temporal sequence compares flowing water with arising and ceasing instant by instant: the former instant ceases and the latter arises.
Three years are retrospectively compared to the interval of an instant.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無一剎那而不受生。無一剎那而不變滅
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhongfeng states that there is no instant without undergoing birth and no instant without change and cessation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 悟即剎那成佛，迷而萬劫輪流
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A verse contrasts becoming a buddha in an instant upon awakening with cycling for myriad ages while confused.
A direct comparison says, “an instant is swift as a finger-snap.”
